frequency_question: How often do federal education authorities proceed all the way to formal revocation of a major professional accreditor's authority within a short policy window?
membership_rule: Includes formal Department of Education proceedings targeting national or professional institutional accreditors that resulted in a final termination order. Excludes voluntary relinquishments, mere compliance warnings, or renewals.

cases.name: American Bar Association accreditation review under Department of Education (1995-1996)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) initial termination (2016)

coverage_note: 3 named; represents the complete set of high-stakes institutional accreditor revocation challenges by the federal government in modern administrative history.
known_gaps: Lower-profile advisory committee recommendations that did not reach a formal Secretarial revocation order are excluded.
skeleton: Total major professional or national accreditor formal revocation proceedings initiated by the Department of Education.
multiplier: 2 hits out of roughly 3 major contested recognition death-penalty proceedings over 30 years.
validity_reason: Administrative law standards and the statutory framework governing the Department of Education's NACIQI process remain stable across presidential administrations.
